what: Claims this project published and then retracted. Machine-read by test_r1_retracted.py, which fails if a retracted claim reappears anywhere in the tree without a pointer to its retraction beside it. Written 2026-09-15 after the conformance claim was corrected in eleven files and survived in five more, including the README front page, because the sweep was a hand-written grep over the phrasings its author happened to think of.
rule: A retracted phrasing may appear ANYWHERE, in any framing, on one condition: the retraction's id must appear within `window` lines of it. Records listed in `allow` are exempt entirely, because their whole purpose is to hold the original wording unedited. A regex cannot tell an assertion from a description of an assertion -- that is a known limit of this project's own judge -- so this check does not try. It requires the citation instead, which is checkable.

retractions.claim: That reproducing the published conformance root is evidence an independent build performed the computation, and that this is NIR's move applied to governance.
retractions.refuted_by: Jens Egholm Pedersen (DTU), 2026-09-15, author of the borrowed idea
retractions.truth: The root is sha256 over the expected outputs printed inside docs/CONFORMANCE_SPEC.json itself, so it reproduces in nine lines with no implementation of climb or attest at all. The real evidence is per-vector: compute each expected from its input and compare. That is an ordinary test-vector suite and pins the computation only where it samples. REPLACED 2026-09-15 by docs/SEMANTICS.md, which states the rules independently of any implementation, with spec_reference.py and test_r2_semantics.py checking them over an exhaustively enumerated space.
verbatim: The root `0c398099...0f0ddcef` is a claim that an independent build, in any language, sharing none of this code, produces the same number.
A matching root means two implementations sharing no code agree; a different one is a finding.
Two builds sharing no code either produce the same root or they do not.
a fork can now prove it agrees without running these exact bytes
so an independent build in any language reproduces the root without reading any Python
Two instances sharing no source can then produce the same conformance root, and an instance that copied the text but broke the behaviour cannot.
patterns: same root or they do not
retractions.note_on_patterns: Deliberately NOT a generic 'same root': test_v1_verifier_agreement.py asserts that three verifiers in three languages produce the same CONSTITUTION hash, which is a different claim and still true. A pattern that convicts it would be a false positive, and a guard that cries wolf gets switched off.

retractions.claim: That a git clone line composed in Gmail arrives usable. It arrives wrapped as a google.com/url redirect and clones an EMPTY repository.
retractions.refuted_by: the sent copies themselves, every letter until 2026-09-15
retractions.truth: Gmail wraps on SEND, not on paste, so checking the draft proves nothing. Verify the sent copy, or use no URLs at all.

retractions.claim: That covenant_route.py's judge runs locally and that the summarise path keeps everything on this machine.
retractions.refuted_by: covenant_route.py's own header after the Ollama removal of 2026-09-12, and public Actions run 35064624218
retractions.truth: There is no local path in covenant_route.py. Every task dispatches to a GitHub Actions runner in the repository resolved from `git remote get-url origin` -- the PUBLIC LAWLESS1987/covenant -- and the runner's job summary is rendered publicly. Run 35064624218 on 2026-09-16 published a readable summary of one of the operator's videos there. The defect was the CLAIM, not the publishing: the operator is not aiming for private, so the tool now ANNOUNCES the destination on every call rather than refusing. COVENANT_HOLD_PRIVATE=1 refuses instead, for material naming a third party (A129).
verbatim: covenant_route.py summarize (local Ollama judge) -> summary + facts
Nothing here uses a cloud model.
retractions.note_on_patterns: Deliberately NARROW. A generic 'local judge' pattern matches 256 places, and almost all are correct: covenant_judge_defer.py's local judge really is local -- the distilled student runs in-process on the node. Only covenant_route.py's path was misdescribed. A guard that convicted all 256 would cry wolf and get switched off, which is the same over-matching that was withdrawn from A121 during construction.

retractions.claim: That raising the ethics judge's margin to convict from 2.4 to 3.0 is strictly worse than leaving it -- that it removes no false convictions AND costs a correct one.
retractions.refuted_by: the nightly retrain of 2026-09-18 03:44, caught the same day by test_a126_seat_dispositions.py's own exam, which is the guard that carried the claim
retractions.truth: On the model of 2026-09-19 the base and margin-3.0 tallies are IDENTICAL -- (38 right, 7 false convictions, 0 wrong clears, 8 abstained) both -- so 3.0 removes nothing and costs nothing. It is a NO-OP, not a trade, which is neither the retracted claim nor the failure the suite warned about. The finding underneath it never moved and is now what the suite pins instead: raising the bar to convict cannot buy a false conviction for free, because all seven false convictions are `discourse` -- text that DESCRIBES a theft rather than committing one -- and the worst of them outscores the mildest true conviction, so no threshold separates the two (A126.M4). Only coverage moves it, at a stated price (A126.M3).
retractions.why_restated_rather_than_left_red: The claim pinned THIS MODEL'S NUMBERS, so every overnight retrain re-broke it: narrowed once on 2026-09-17 after a student promotion, broken again on 2026-09-18. A claim rewritten whenever the judge moves is following the judge around rather than holding it to anything, and a permanently red line teaches its reader to skip the place a real failure would appear (A60). The replacement constrains margins 3.0 and 3.5 together at EVERY tally either could produce, which is strictly harder to satisfy than the two single-tally assertions it replaces, and A126.M1c drives the predicate to a failing verdict so the guard has been watched failing.
retractions.the_other_perspective: Branch `a126-margin-claim-as-written-2026-09-19` holds the tree with the claim exactly as written, at commit c1ffb9c, pushed to origin. `git checkout a126-margin-claim-as-written-2026-09-19 && python test_a126_seat_dispositions.py` runs the older reading against WHATEVER MODEL IS ON DISK THAT DAY. It scored 10/12 against fallback_model.json as retrained at 2026-09-18 03:44; fallback_model.json is rewritten nightly, so a later run may score differently -- and that is not a flaw in the record, it is the measurement the record exists to make available. Nothing about the restatement is hidden behind a rewrite of history: the case for the older, stronger reading can still be run.
verbatim: margin 3.0 still removes NO false convictions and costs a correct one -- strictly worse on both counts
...and it costs correct convictions, so it is worse on both counts
retractions.note_on_patterns: Deliberately narrow. A pattern over 'margin 3.0' alone matches the measurement lines, the restated comment and every transcript that ever printed the exam, none of which reassert anything. These two phrases are the ASSERTION and appear nowhere else in the tree.
retractions.note_on_allow: The three added files are SWEEP TRANSCRIPTS: a verbatim record of what the suite printed on a given day, which is the one kind of file whose whole purpose is to hold the old wording unedited. Editing a transcript to satisfy a guard would be falsifying the record the guard exists to protect. Same reasoning as A121's docs/RUN_LOG_ARCHIVE.md. ONE_RUN.txt is overwritten by the next sweep and will carry the restated wording by itself; the other two are archives and will not.

retractions.claim: That today's daily trading plan is approved by the operator -- asserted as a property of the money gate, in test_g4_money_gates.py G4.4b.
retractions.refuted_by: the sweep of 2026-09-19 at 09:20, run before the operator had approved that morning: G4 16/17, 'no approved daily plan for 2026-09-19'. The same check was 17/17 in all three sweeps of 2026-09-18, taken after his 07:10:50 approval.
retractions.truth: Whether today is approved is a fact about the operator's morning, not about the gate. ops/daily_approvals.jsonl records an approval for 2026-09-15, -16, -17 and -18 and none for the 19th at the time of the sweep; the gate refused correctly, and the check called that refusal a failure. Left as written it would go red every morning until he taps and green after -- a suite reporting his to-do list as a test failure, on the money path, which is A60's defect in the worst place for it: a line red by routine is a line nobody reads on the day it means something. The gate itself was never wrong and is not changed by this.
retractions.why_restated_rather_than_left_red: The invariant the original author wanted is that the gate READS the decision rather than assuming one, and that is now driven both ways: G4.4 against a day with no approval, G4.4b against the most recent day the ledger says was approved. It is strictly more than the old form measured -- the old one could pass on a day the gate was broken but the operator happened to have approved. The no-data branch is explicit and fails: pointed at an empty approvals ledger the check reports NOT MEASURED and takes G4 to 16/17 rather than passing on absence, which is the fake-guard shape this project has already paid for twice (A65, A74).
retractions.the_other_perspective: Branch `g4-daily-plan-check-as-written-2026-09-19` holds the tree at f6ae5d6 with the check exactly as written, pushed to origin. Run it before the operator's morning approval and it fails; run it after and it passes -- which is the behaviour being retracted, reproducible on demand.
verbatim: G4.4b ...today, which the operator approved from the phone, is not
retractions.note_on_patterns: One pattern, narrow. A pattern over 'daily plan' or 'approved' matches the gate's own refusal strings, the plan store, the route and every transcript, none of which assert anything about today. This phrase is the assertion.
retractions.note_on_allow: The four added files are sweep transcripts -- a verbatim record of what the suite printed on a given day, the one kind of file whose purpose is to hold the old wording unedited. test_g4_money_gates.py is deliberately NOT allowed: it quotes the retracted sentence in the comment explaining the retraction, and cites G4b two lines above it, so containment covers it. That is the rule working as intended rather than being waived.

retractions.claim: That three private node keys (covenant_A.db.key, nodeA_run.db.key, nodeB_run.db.key) sit in a folder that syncs to the cloud and have already left the machine -- INDEX.md, audited 2026-08-20, the page's opening section.
retractions.refuted_by: Measurement on 2026-09-26, names and attributes only, no key opened: the covenant folder is not under the OneDrive root, is not a junction, its key files carry no cloud attributes, Desktop and Documents are not redirected, and no copy exists under OneDrive or the Syncthing folder; .gitignore line 4 (*.key) ignores all three, and no .key file was ever added on any ref.
retractions.truth: The three files are still in the covenant folder (dated 2026-08-19, never moved; a copy of covenant_A.db.key also sits in ~/.covenant-keys/), and by every measure taken that folder does not sync to the cloud and git never carried them. Moving them is still the operator's decision, because covenant_A.db.key is bound to covenant_A.db. Not measured: other backup tools, and where the files were before 2026-09-26.
retractions.why_restated_rather_than_left_red: The original warning is kept in INDEX.md as it was published, with a dated correction beside it -- the rule in docs/CORRECTIONS.md. This entry makes that correction load-bearing: the warning's phrasings may appear only within the window of an A33 citation.
retractions.the_other_perspective: The warning's habit is sound and stays: nothing secret should live in the repository folder. What was wrong is the stated fact (that the folder syncs, and that the keys had left). The same belief remains in EXCHANGE_SETUP.md:28 and in two scripts' refusal messages; it is listed under 'What has not been corrected' in docs/CORRECTIONS.md rather than patterned here.
verbatim: ## FIX THIS FIRST — three private keys are in a folder that leaves your machine
This folder syncs to the cloud. Anything in it has already left your computer.
retractions.note_on_patterns: Two patterns, both the page's own wording. A pattern over 'syncs to the cloud' would also match EXCHANGE_SETUP.md and the two balance scripts, which state the same belief as the reason for a refusal that is sound on its own; those are recorded as uncorrected instead of being made to carry a citation they would not explain.
retractions.note_on_allow: The record files, and the sweep transcripts that print what the suite read, as for G4b. INDEX.md is deliberately NOT allowed: it keeps the original text, so it must carry the A33 citation within the window.
